newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan money rates end lower, seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan money rates end lower, seen rising.

text.p: Pakistan's money market rates traded at lower levels on Wednesday amid excess liquidity but dealers said a huge outflow on settlement of an auction was likely to push the rates up on Thursday.
"The overnight market traded in the range of 1.50 percent and four percent," a dealer at Standard Chartered Bank said.
The State (central) Bank of Pakistan (SBP) picked up one billion rupees in its weekly open market operation but could not move the market up because of excess liquidity, he said.

He said the rates were likely to rise on Thursday amid settlement of an auction of six-month short-term federal bonds worth 13.463 billion rupees against an inflow of 6.2 billion rupees on the maturity of an earlier auction.
